people.name: Andrés Cibils
people.bio: Rangeland scientist who directs the USDA Southern Plains Climate Hub, based at the ARS Grazinglands Research Laboratory in El Reno, Oklahoma. Earlier he was a USDA-NIFA National Program Leader for climate change and a range science professor at New Mexico State University, studying heritage Criollo cattle and precision ranching on arid rangelands.
people.research_interests: resilient rangeland-based livestock systems; rangeland ecology; climate-smart agriculture

people.name: Susan Eisenhour
people.bio: Program Specialist and coordinator of the USDA Southern Plains Climate Hub at ARS in El Reno, Oklahoma, previously a program support assistant at the host Grazinglands Research Laboratory. She coordinates Hub partnerships and its K-12 education work with STEM partners, drawing on experience in project coordination, grant management and workshop organization.

people.name: Alex Krichels
people.bio: Dryland ecosystem ecologist named Forest Service co-lead of the Hub while a research ecologist in the USFS Rocky Mountain Research Station dryland ecosystems program in Albuquerque. Trained at the University of Illinois, with a UC Riverside postdoc, he studies how drought, fire and nitrogen deposition alter dryland carbon and nitrogen cycling.
people.research_interests: dryland ecosystems; carbon and nitrogen cycling; drought, wildfire and nitrogen deposition disturbance

people.name: Jean L. Steiner
people.bio: Agroclimatologist with a Kansas State University PhD who spent most of her career as a USDA-ARS researcher, ending as head of the ARS Grazinglands Research Laboratory at El Reno, Oklahoma. Now a KSU adjunct professor and senior research partnerships coordinator, she studies how climate affects water and agricultural ecosystems.
people.research_interests: water resources and climate impacts in agroecosystems; evapotranspiration; crop residue management; watershed management; integrated agroecosystems

people.name: Mati Mohammadi
people.bio: Agricultural economist and postdoctoral researcher at Texas A&M University-Kingsville serving as a Southern Plains Climate Hub fellow. With a Purdue PhD, she is building system dynamics models of climate vulnerability for regional beef and wheat production and supply chains.
people.research_interests: agricultural economics; system dynamics modeling; beef and wheat supply chains under climate change

people.name: Xavier A. Jaime
people.bio: Ecologist and Texas A&M University postdoctoral associate working as a Southern Plains Climate Hub fellow, synthesizing evidence on NRCS conservation practices and greenhouse gas mitigation and modeling agrivoltaics suitability on rangelands. His doctoral work used remote sensing to study fire effects in Texas mesquite-oak savannas.
people.research_interests: rangeland and fire ecology; remote sensing; conservation practices; agrivoltaics

people.name: Clay Pope
people.bio: Outreach consultant who carried out climate literacy outreach for the USDA Southern Plains Climate Hub from its 2014 founding until 2023 under NRCS-ARS agreements, through blogs, a podcast and regional events, before moving to partnership outreach and policy work with The Nature Conservancy in Oklahoma.
